key_insight: GRASP learns probabilistic logic programs by using functional gradient boosting and an LLM as a proposal oracle to generate first-order rules, making symbolic structure learning more scalable and interpretable.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical neurosymbolic route for relational modeling tasks where exhaustive symbolic search is too costly, while still producing transparent weighted rule ensembles.
method: Frame rule induction as functional gradient boosting over probabilistic logic programs.
Use an LLM to propose candidate first-order rules instead of brute-force combinatorial search.
Combine proposed rules into an interpretable weighted ensemble that fits relational distributions.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on four relational benchmarks, including Tox21, mutagenesis, and Cora, and is reported to outperform symbolic, neural, and LLM-only baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and reliability of LLM-proposed hypotheses, so weak proposals or prompt/search design could limit gains and reproducibility.
paper_title: Learning Probabilistic Logic Programs with Functional Gradient Guided Language Models
